name: Said Reklaoui
headline: AI Engineer · LLMs, agents & ML in production
tagline: I build products with AI in them, and I build them with AI.
summary: AI Engineer. For the last three years almost everything I build has a model doing real work in it: classifiers and fine-tuned LLMs for customer support, LLM pipelines with structured output and cost control, agents over MCP, and open models I serve myself on GPUs. I also build my own products (an AI code reviewer, a sim-racing telemetry app and a meeting copilot) and I build them with coding agents, end to end. What I've learned doing it: the model is the easy part. Evaluation, real data, cost and tests are what make it hold up, and that's where fifteen years of backend engineering pays off.
ai_focus: LLM apps · structured output · tool calling

projects.name: CodeGuard — AI code review (my own product)
projects.description: Reviews pull requests against each team's own rules, written in plain prose, not a generic linter's. Specialised agents run in parallel over structured code context, then a verification pass drops what doesn't hold up. I served the models myself first (Qwen3-Coder 30B → Qwen3.6-35B MoE, FP8, vLLM on RunPod serverless GPUs): moving from Ollama to vLLM took throughput from 78 to 226 tok/s at 5 concurrent reviews, with 128k context on a 96 GB GPU and the image cut from 164 GB to 40 GB for faster cold starts. A golden-corpus bench measures recall and precision, and the cost per review it measured is what later moved inference to hosted models behind a price-routed gateway. Built with coding agents: 670+ commits and 1,700+ tests that run in under a minute.
projects.tech: Python, vLLM, RunPod, Qwen, OpenRouter, AI Agents, Evaluation, MongoDB, React, Docker

projects.name: RaceIQ Live — sim-racing telemetry (my own product)
projects.description: Live overlay and post-session analysis for iRacing: it tells you where you gain or lose time against any reference lap you pick. Turns 60 Hz telemetry from every car into laps, sectors and a continuous distance→time delta; lap times match iRacing's own within 2 ms, and the tests replay real recorded sessions instead of mocks. A scheduled agent reviews every new recording on its own, audits it and opens the issue and the fix. Next up is Coach, an AI agent that reads your telemetry and tells you which corners cost you time. ~200 commits in three weeks, built with coding agents.
projects.tech: Python, Time-series telemetry, Tauri, AI Agents, GitHub Actions, Windows installer

projects.name: Sotto — AI meeting copilot (my own product)
projects.description: Desktop app that transcribes meetings live, suggests what to answer and files each one with notes. Speech runs locally with Whisper (~0.4 s per chunk on GPU), and a small local model decides in ~0.2 s whether someone actually asked you something before a bigger model writes the answer, so you only pay when it matters. Semantic search over past meetings, MCP both ways (a client with OAuth 2.1 to Gmail, Slack, Linear and others, asking before any write, and its own MCP server so Claude can query your meetings) and cost tracked per day. Linux, Windows and macOS builds from CI. Built with coding agents.
projects.tech: Python, Whisper, Qwen3 4B (local), OpenRouter, MCP, Embeddings, GitHub Actions
